The Willowbrook Animal Shelter announced plans this week to expand its facility, nearly doubling its capacity to care for homeless pets in the region. The $3 million expansion will include additional kennels, an expanded veterinary clinic, and a new outdoor play area for dogs.

Shelter director Alan Reyes said the expansion has been years in the making, driven by consistently high intake numbers that have often left the shelter operating beyond capacity. Construction is expected to begin this winter and take approximately one year to complete.

The shelter is currently accepting donations to help fund the project and has set a goal of raising $500,000 from the community before construction begins.

Dear Fleet Drivers,

This is a reminder that all company vehicles are due for their quarterly inspection this month. Please schedule an appointment with the maintenance garage at your earliest convenience, as slots tend to fill up quickly toward the end of the month.

During the inspection, technicians will check tire condition, brakes, fluid levels, and overall vehicle safety. Any vehicle that fails inspection will be taken out of service until repairs are completed.

Please bring your vehicle's logbook to the appointment so mileage and maintenance history can be updated accordingly.

Thank you for helping us keep our fleet safe and reliable.

We are excited to announce the opening of a new employee reading corner on the fourth floor, stocked with a variety of business, self-development, and leisure books donated by staff and management. The space includes comfortable seating and is available for use during breaks or after hours.

Employees are welcome to borrow books on an honor system; simply take a book and return it once finished, or feel free to leave a note recommending it to others. We also welcome donations of gently used books to help grow the collection.

We hope this new space provides a quiet spot to unwind and encourages a culture of continuous learning among our team.

City engineers announced a two-phase plan to repair the aging Fifth Street Bridge, a key route used by thousands of commuters daily. The first phase, focused on structural reinforcement, will begin next month and require partial lane closures during off-peak hours.

The second phase, which includes resurfacing and improved lighting, is scheduled for next spring. City officials say the entire project is necessary to extend the bridge's lifespan by at least 25 years and avoid a costly full replacement.

Drivers are advised to expect minor delays during the first phase and to consider alternate routes when possible.

choices: To extend the bridge's lifespan by at least 25 years

Skyline Café, the city's first rooftop garden café, opened to the public last week atop the newly renovated Meridian Building downtown. The café features an urban garden where much of its produce is grown on-site, along with panoramic views of the city skyline.

Owner Lena Park said the concept was inspired by her desire to bring more green space into the city's dense downtown core. In addition to food and drinks, the café hosts weekly gardening workshops for the public, teaching skills such as composting and container gardening.

Park hopes the café will encourage other building owners in the area to consider similar rooftop developments in the future.
